result.summary: The protocol is careful, leakage control is credible and the numbers reproduce from results/raw_results.csv.gz. Seen from a competing group, though, the central claim does not hold up against the authors' own result files: "pseudo-count shrinkage of the score distribution is the most reliable strategy" for newly metered buildings. (1) A zero-parameter rule beats the headline HSC-CQR. The rule uses pooled CQR for the first week and self-only CQR after that. I rebuilt it from per-building coverage_early/coverage_late, which is exact because Self-CQR's late radius depends only on the building's own scores. (2) The whole gain comes after week 1. In week 1 the headline method under-covers as often as plain CQR, which contradicts the claim that it is reliable "throughout onboarding". (3) ACI, the main online competitor, is limited by an edge-case convention that removes its competitive step sizes from tuning. (4) The headline variant includes components the paper itself calls useless. It is also beaten by an untuned fixed-κ variant, because the selection objective (interval score) does not match the stated goal (reliability). The real finding, that a building's own errors should take over after about a week, is useful but incremental. It also needs to be shown against the trivial switching baseline and a fairly configured ACI. All checks were read-only; scratch analysis ran on results/raw_results.csv.gz and results/run_info.json.

issues.title: A trivial switching rule (pooled CQR in week 1, then Self-CQR) matches or beats HSC-CQR
issues.evidence: Built from results/raw_results.csv.gz (exp=main, alpha=0.1, perturb=none), per-building coverage = (7*coverage_early[CQR] + 49*coverage_late[Self-CQR])/56. This is exact for coverage because the Self-CQR radius after day 7 uses only own scores. Results, mean ± s.d. over seeds. BDG2: MACD 0.0163±0.0006, under-covered 2.7±0.9%; HSC-CQR 0.0176±0.0010, 3.4±0.8%. UCI: 0.0130±0.0015, 0.4±0.6%; HSC-CQR 0.0136, 0.6%. Median relative IS of the rule (rebuilt from rel_IS/rel_IS_early): 0.568 vs 0.564 on BDG2 and 0.367 vs 0.368 on UCI. The 7-day boundary is the pre-specified EARLY=7 (src/evaluation/metrics.py:15), not a value tuned after seeing the results. Self-CQR loses to HSC-CQR only because of its week-1 behaviour (early coverage 0.864, week-1 under-covered share 33.7%). Self-CQR switches to own scores as soon as n>=9 (src/models/calibration.py:84-87), i.e. from day 2 with 24 scores.
issues.action: Add Self-CQR with a minimum-history fallback, e.g. pooled CQR until h=7 or until n>=168 own scores, as a baseline in Tables 2-5 and 7 and in the paired tests. Either show that HSC-CQR beats it, or reframe the contribution as 'switch to or blend in own scores after about a week' and drop the claim that the score-distribution mixture is superior.
issues.experiment: Re-run the calibration stage only (no retraining): Self-CQR with fallback thresholds {72, 168, 336} h, chosen by LOBO on calibration buildings, on all protocols and stress tests.

issues.title: ACI is held back by the a<=0 convention, which removes its competitive step sizes from tuning
issues.evidence: aci_quantiles (src/models/calibration.py:229) sets the radius to the grid maximum (500 s) whenever 1-a>=1. Because each day applies a batched update of 24 errors, any gamma>=0.002 makes the LOBO objective blow up. results/run_info.json main_BDG2_s0_a0.1 tune_aci_cqr: obj 0.224 at gamma=0.001, 1.51 at 0.002, 15.0 at 0.005, 56.8 at 0.01 (UCI: 0.191 -> 6.14 at 0.005). The selected gamma (0.0002-0.002) is 2.5-25 times below the usual 0.005 of Gibbs & Candès, so the text's 'adapts more slowly because ... small step size' (Sec. 5.2, 6.1) is caused by the convention, not by the method. The same artefact appears on target buildings: Table 4 ACI-CQR IS mean difference -0.17 [CI -0.505, -0.002] on BDG2 and -1.91 [-4.60, -0.15] on UCI.
issues.action: Use a finite radius when a<=0, e.g. the largest calibration score or the pooled 1-alpha/10 quantile, or clip a_t to [alpha/10, 1]. Alternatively use per-hour updates or an aggregated/strongly-adaptive ACI. Retune gamma and report ACI-CQR again. Also report ACI tuned for coverage deviation.
issues.experiment: Calibration-stage re-run of ACI-CQR (and ACI) with clipped levels across the gamma grid, on main, LSO and stress protocols.

issues.title: No improvement in the first week: the onboarding claim is not supported
issues.evidence: Week-1 per-building coverage (coverage_early, h<=7) on BDG2: share below 0.85 is CQR 23.8%, HSC-CQR 24.5%, HSC-CQR simple 21.7%, fixed-κ 19.8%. On UCI: CQR 16.0%, HSC-CQR 17.5%. Table 2 week-1 mean coverage is 0.885 for HSC-CQR vs 0.892 for CQR. Even so, Sec. 6.3 says the layer 'keeps the share of buildings with clearly unreliable intervals small throughout onboarding', and the abstract and conclusion rest on newly metered buildings. Late-window MACD (h>7) is HSC-CQR 0.0196 vs Self-CQR 0.0229, so the reported 56-day gains are concentrated in weeks 2-8.
issues.action: Report per-building metrics by window (week 1, weeks 2-4, weeks 5-8) in the main tables and state the week-1 failure in the abstract and conclusion. Remove 'throughout onboarding'. Discuss the sampling-noise floor for 168-hour coverage.
issues.experiment: None; a re-analysis of the existing results is enough.

issues.title: The headline method includes components declared unnecessary, and the tuning objective does not match the stated goal
issues.evidence: The abstract and highlights report full HSC-CQR (kNN + stage matching): 3.4% / 0.018. Yet Table 5 has simple at 2.9% / 0.017 and the untuned fixed-κ=168 at 1.9% / 0.015 (BDG2), and fixed-κ beats tuned HSC-CQR in paired tests (r_rb=-0.45, p<0.001). On leave-site-out, simple gives 3.5% vs full 5.3%. LOBO on IS picks κ=336 (run_info hsc_cqr_simple), while target MACD is lowest at 96-168 (Sec. 5.7). The 'most reliable strategy' claim therefore depends on which variant is labelled HSC-CQR.
issues.action: Make the one-parameter simple variant the reported method, as the paper itself recommends. Choose κ with an objective that matches the stated goal, e.g. LOBO MACD or IS plus an under-coverage penalty, or state that it is pre-specified. Add paired tests of full vs simple to back the claim that the components 'add nothing'.
issues.experiment: Calibration-stage LOBO re-selection with a reliability-oriented objective.

issues.title: The HSC vs QShrink comparison mixes the mechanism with the selected pseudo-count
issues.evidence: LOBO objectives are almost the same (BDG2 s0: QShrink best 0.59636 at λ=672; HSC simple best 0.59560 at κ=336). QShrink mostly selects λ=672-1344 while HSC selects κ=336, and target reliability gets better with smaller pseudo-counts (Fig. 9). The claimed 'advantage for the distribution mixture' (Sec. 6.1) may therefore come from the selected value rather than the mechanism. Table 4: QShrink IS difference not significant (p=0.688 and 0.277). results/sensitivity.csv covers only HSC.
issues.action: Compare HSC and QShrink at matched pseudo-counts (the full λ/κ grid on targets, plus fixed 168), or soften the claim.
issues.experiment: Target-side sensitivity grid for QShrink-CQR (calibration stage only).

issues.title: Stress-test text overstates HSC's advantage
issues.evidence: Table 6, meter noise 15%: Self-CQR 0.010 / 0% vs HSC-CQR 0.018 / 2%. Cal. pool 10%: QShrink 0.019 / 6 vs HSC-CQR 0.020 / 8. Cal. pool 50%: QShrink 0.019 / 3. The conclusion still says the layer 'remained beneficial' in a way that suggests it was the best option under stress.
issues.action: State which method is best in each stress condition, and add the switching baseline to Table 6.
issues.experiment: Included in the re-run for issue 1.

issues.title: No Mondrian baseline on CQR scores
issues.evidence: Mondrian-usage is reported only for absolute scores (Table 2, 28.5%), so it cannot be compared with the CQR-based strategies that drive the conclusions.
issues.action: Add Mondrian-usage-CQR, or state why it was left out.
issues.experiment: Calibration stage only.
